question: Why did the dilepton invariant mass distribution give the most precise top quark mass of the individual fixed-order fits?
question_long: In the ATLAS measurement of lepton distributions in ttbar events at 8 TeV, why did the dilepton invariant mass distribution give the most precise top quark mass of the individual fixed-order fits?
expect: premise false: m^emu gives the least precise determination, 174.5 +5.1 -5.3 GeV (Table 15 and text)
trap: explaining why it is most precise
rendered: The dilepton invariant mass distribution gave the most precise top quark mass of the individual fixed-order fits because it is sensitive to the top quark mass in a way that is complementary to the traditional measurements of m t using the invariant mass of the reconstructed top quark decay products.

prompt.system: You answer questions about one document, "Measurement of lepton differential distributions and the top quark mass in ttbar production in pp collisions at sqrt(s) = 8 TeV with the ATLAS detector", using only what that document contains.
